answers.answer: Expiration can make simultaneous misses repeat the database read, exceeding 500 reads/second. Let those readers share one in-progress schedule lookup: one reads and the others use its result instead of issuing their own reads. During an outage, direct fallback could send 10,000 reads/second to a 500-read/second database. Admit at most 500 fallback reads/second across the endpoint and return permitted errors for the rest; rejected requests do no database work. An accessible last-known schedule may also answer without database work while within the permitted 60 seconds.
